subject: Resize trajectory and pricing bridge for Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Sana Malik <sana@zephyrus.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Zephyrus Procurement <procurement@zephyrus.ai>
Date: 2027-06-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity planning: pool increase & throughput SLOs

Hi Ava,

Hope you
re well. We're approaching our mid-year forecast and expect a steady 45% increase in LLM traffic over the next 3 months for production traffic (inference + embeddings). Current pool is 8 A100 GPUs on Dedicated; our team is concerned about sustained 99th percentile latency once we hit the new load.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a mid-term uplift path (add GPUs to the same pool mid-contract) and confirm whether throughput guarantees (tokens/sec per GPU) would scale linearly for our workload?
- What's the pricing impact: do you offer a pro-rated commit for top-ups vs. just paying on-demand? Any flexibility on list discount for a mid-term increase?

I've attached a short usage export for the last 90 days so you can see the pattern.

Can we get a proposal by next Tuesday? We
 like to share with procurement too.

Thanks,
Sana Malik
Head of ML Engineering
Zephyrus AI

Attachment: Zephyrus_MLPool_Usage_Report.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB, summary CSV inside)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sana Malik <sana@zephyrus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning: pool increase & throughput SLOs

Thanks Sana — got the report and context. Appreciate the heads-up on the trajectory. Quick answers up-front: yes, we support mid-contract pool top-ups (add GPUs to an existing Dedicated pool) and we can offer a structured pro-rated commit so you
 get committed-rate pricing for the added capacity rather than pure on-demand. Throughput per GPU does not strictly scale perfectly linearly in all workloads, but for your seq-len and request pattern (we reviewed the attached), we expect near-linear scaling with continuous batching and KV cache.

I'll pull together two concrete paths: a conservative top-up (add 4 GPUs now, review after 60 days) and an accelerated path (add 8 GPUs now with a stepped commit). Karthik and Marcus will help with pricing tiers and the exact SLO language.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday 6/27 at 10:00am PT to walk through options?

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Ava Chen
Redwood Inference

From: Sana Malik <sana@zephyrus.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-25T13:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning: pool increase & throughput SLOs

On 6/25/27 11:03 AM, Ava Chen wrote:
> Thanks Sana  

Yes, Thursday 6/27 10:00am PT works for the ML team.

Quick note from procurement side: if we go with a mid-term uplift, procurement will ask for a one-time onboarding credit for the uplift and a 12-month blended commit instead of immediate repricing to a longer-term step-up. Can you indicate typical concession levels for a first top-up mid-contract?

Sana

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing options for Zephyrus mid-term top-up

Ava / Marcus,

I reviewed the usage export and sketched three options we can offer. High level (tradeoffs: discount vs. SLO strength vs. yes/no pro-rate):

Option A - Conservative top-up - Add 4 GPUs (A100 eq) to existing pool immediately - Pro-rated commit for remaining term (prorate of months remaining) - 10% discount off list for the added commit - Throughput SLO: maintain baseline 95th p99 token latency target; no additional 99th guarantee until post 60 day calibration

Option B - Stepped commit (recommended for predictable growth) - Add 8 GPUs (burst now, reserve 4 for the next 90 days) - 12-month blended commit for the newly reserved capacity (gives procurement the 12-month blended they asked for) - 17% discount off list for the blended commit - Throughput SLO: 99p latency target guaranteed after a 30-day stabilization window; interim capacity fallback policy included

Option C - Full renewal uplift (best economics) - Requote entire Dedicated pool at new size (move from 8->16 GPUs) - Annual commit starting on amendment effective date; 24% discount off list - Strong throughput SLA (99p) with financial credits for SLA misses

Attachments: pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-GPU unit rates and pro-rate math).

Notes: procurement will push for higher discount and a go/no-go credit for the uplift. We have some room to move on Option B (up to 20% if we secure a multi-year clause), and Option C needs legal sign-off due to SLA credits.

Happy to sync on the call and present Option B as our primary path.

-Karthik
Director, Renewals & Growth
Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sana Malik <sana@zephyrus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: stepped commit path (Option B) and draft amendment

Hi Sana — thanks for the call last week. Per our discussion, attached is the draft amendment outlining Option B (stepped commit) with the blended 12-month pricing for the reserved portion and a pro-rated invoicing approach for the immediate top-up. Highlights: 

- Immediate add: 8 GPUs to the existing pool (4 reserved, 4 billed at pro-rated committed rate for remaining term) - Blended 12-month commit: the 4 reserved GPUs will be billed as a 12-month commit (gives procurement the 12-month blended they requested) - Discount: 17% off list for the blended commit; we can move to 19% if Zephyrus signs a 24-month extension clause at amendment signature - Throughput SLA: 99p latency warranty after a 30-day stabilization window; interim fallback to adjacent region cap if we detect sustained degradation - Onboarding credit: one-time $10k uplift credit applied to the first invoice for the added GPUs (to help cover migration/tuning)

Attachment: Draft_Amendment_ZP-2027-071.pdf; pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (for transparency).

Next step: if this looks acceptable, I'll route the amendment to Legal and prepare a DocuSign envelope for signatures. If procurement wants alternative credit math, ask them to return a redline and we can quickly iterate.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Draft_Amendment_ZP-2027-071.pdf (pdf, 6 pages)
Attachment: pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 23KB)

From: Sana Malik <sana@zephyrus.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Zephyrus Procurement <procurement@zephyrus.ai>
Date: 2027-07-02T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: stepped commit path (Option B) and draft amendment

Ava / Karthik — thanks, this matches the points we discussed. Procurement will review the draft amendment this afternoon. Quick confirmation requests from our side before routing to PO: 

1) Please confirm the effective date used for pro-rate math (we prefer amendment effective date = 2027-07-10).
2) Will the $10k onboarding credit be visible as a separate line item on the first invoice?
3) If we sign the 24-month extension to reach 19% discount, can you confirm there are no additional early-exit penalties beyond the standard termination language?

If those are confirmed, we
 like to proceed and should have procurement issue a PO by next week. Appreciate the onboarding credit — that helps.

Sana Malik
Head of ML Engineering
Zephyrus AI
